payload.label: Check pages at every width and device setting
payload.job: Open each page I give at every width and device setting and read every piece of text a person can see, refusing text that cannot be read, is drawn in a font the page did not ask for, is cut off or makes a phone scroll sideways
payload.description: Opens each of screens (each { id, html, route?, fonts?, ready?, steps?, widths?, modes? }) in a headless Chromium through Playwright (headless-browser/launch.mjs, with its quiet switches and one-browser-at-a-time admission), at every width of views.json (phone 390x844 with no sideways scroll, tablet, desktop) and in every mode (light, dark, forced colours, Dark Reader), or the widths and modes asked for, through runMatrix (check-screens.mjs). The page's HTML is answered by the browser itself at its route on a made-up origin; any other request the page makes is aborted, never sent. Each view is scrolled window by window and every visible text node is judged: contrast under WCAG AA against the colour really behind it, a glyph drawn by a platform font the screen does not declare in fonts (system names such as system-ui never count), text cut off or outside the window, a phone page wider than its window, and a control with no accessible name; a screen that does not open is a failure. allowlist (allowlist.json's shape, none when left out) drops a proven false positive or keeps a decided look as reported. Answers passed, failures ({ screen, width, mode, probe, selector, text, detail }), reported, counts (failures per probe) and report (views read, texts read, seconds per phase). Writes no file and keeps nothing; needs a Chromium Playwright can find. Refuses a screen without an id or html, two screens at one route, and a width or mode views.json does not name. The deploy check also opens a live origin or a Worker, takes pictures of failures, runs the real Dark Reader extension and refuses a deploy; this run checks only the pages given.

provenance.source: Trillion-X/trillion tools/check-every-screen-at-every-width/check-screens.mjs, in-page.mjs, views.json, allowlist.json and vendor/darkreader.js, moved in a9ee258 (#76); old capability row capabilities.json:558 at 4ffa1dc4a2^ (open every screen at every width and device setting and read every piece of text a person can see, before going live). check-given-pages.mjs is new: it serves the given pages inside the browser and runs runMatrix over them.

payload.label: Check live screens on a phone and a computer
payload.job: Open each live page at its real address the way a person's phone and computer open it, and measure how long it takes to first show, to be usable, its longest task, its console errors and failed requests; tap the controls named and say whether each did what it expects; keep a picture of each screen in the person's Files
payload.description: Opens each of pages (each { id, url, old_url?, sign_in?, ready?, taps? }) in a headless Chromium through Playwright (headless-browser/launch.mjs, with its quiet switches and one-browser-at-a-time admission) at each view of views.json (phone 390x844, tablet, desktop; all when left out, or the views asked for). Each view is a cold load in its own browser context. The phone has its CPU and network slowed as live-screens.json names (DATA); the desktop has none. For each page and view it answers: status, first_paint_ms, first_contentful_paint_ms, usable_ms (the ready selector is visible and the main thread has been idle for usable_idle_ms), blank_ms (until the screen first shows any text, picture or control), longest_task_ms, console_errors, failed_requests, and picture (the full screen as PNG, kept in the person's Files under /live-screens/<run>/ and returned by its 1f: identity; a picture the Files right cannot keep is returned as base64 when small). The same for old_url when given. taps are made on the new side after its load, one after another; each reports worked, ms, detail and a picture. It judges nothing: the caller compares the numbers with its own bar. A sign_in is either cookies the caller already holds, or { kind: 'email-code', origin, email, code }: the code the site emailed (the caller sent the request for it), exchanged here for the session cookie. Cookies and codes are never printed or returned. reach steps (taps and waits) run after load and sign-in; the screen's usable time is then measured from the last reach tap, and load_usable_ms keeps the time from the page's load. A URL in the answer has its query removed. A view not begun by until is answered as skipped. Refuses a page without an id or url, a non-http address, a view views.json does not name, and an expect with no known key.

code.description: the six-digit code the site emailed; the caller sent the request for it

reach.description: Steps after load and sign-in, before the screen is measured: taps (sidebar links) and waits

ready.description: A CSS selector that must be visible before the page is usable

until.description: Epoch milliseconds; a view not begun by then is answered as skipped

provenance.source: lane-live-tool (group 9): check-live-screens.mjs and live-screens.json are new; the browser, the views and the reads come from check-given-pages.mjs, check-screens.mjs, in-page.mjs and views.json (tools/check-every-screen-at-every-width).
